# FAQ bank

Questions the public asks more than twice get an approved answer here, so every
channel answers the same question the same way and nobody improvises a claim under
time pressure.

**What does the product actually do?** The approved short answer states the
operational job in one sentence, names the practitioner it serves, and stops. The
long answer adds the three most common deployment shapes with one sentence each.
Neither version contains a superlative.

**How is this different from the obvious alternative?** The approved answer names
the genuine trade-off both directions — what the alternative does better, what we do
better, and the workload shape that decides it. Comparison questions are where
overreach happens; the bank exists mostly for these.

**Can it handle our scale?** The approved answer states the largest measured
configuration with its measurement window, then says plainly that beyond it we have
projections, not measurements. Evaluators respect the boundary; the bank keeps
enthusiasm from moving it.

**What does it cost?** Pricing answers route to the published pricing page and stop.
Discount speculation, negotiation framing, and cost comparisons with competitors are
not answered in public by anyone.

**What about the incident last quarter?** Incident questions get the published
retrospective link and the one-sentence approved summary. Nothing beyond the
retrospective is said in public, however friendly the thread.

Answers are reviewed when their underlying facts change and re-dated here; an answer
older than its facts is a liability wearing a badge. New recurring questions enter
through the channel owner who keeps meeting them, with the approved answer drafted
under the evidence standards before first use.

## Questions we decline

Some recurring questions have an approved non-answer. Roadmap questions get the
published roadmap link and nothing about unlisted work, because a hallway roadmap
answer becomes a commitment the moment it is screenshotted. Questions about
individual customers get a polite decline whatever the sentiment, positive included:
praising one customer in public tells every other customer we talk about them.
Questions about staffing, hiring, or internal process route to the people who own
those answers and are not answered by conversation accounts at all.

## Tone of bank answers

Bank answers are written to sound like a person, reviewed to be exact like a
document. Each one is redrafted whenever three uses in a row required improvised
softening — recurring improvisation means the approved wording reads wrong in real
threads, and the fix belongs in the bank, not in the thread.
